basis_words: Window 2026-10-01 to 2026-10-13, as the order names. Household: the lowest-sha256 household with two or more accounts in the private account dimension (221 such households were eligible); its Orion household id is the dimension household_id as an integer, the rule orion_account_mapping.py applies, and the first account in sorted order fills the vendor account field. Calls 1 and 2 posted the wrapped body from requests_for and both drew HTTP 400. Amendment 1 then posted the inner scope only: calls 3 and 4 drew HTTP 200 on the flag false and the flag true. Response shape, in node-type words: a top object carrying calculations, asOfDate, dataLastUpdated and sessionId; four calculated-group nodes with grouping Account, each holding calculated-performance, calculated-performance-breakdown, calculated-activity and calculated-list nodes, with performance-breakdown-twr points carrying factor and feeAmount fields. The one-account limit is the estate's code, not the vendor's: orion_account_mapping.py refuses a household holding other than one account, yet the vendor returned Account groups for this five-account household, so the vendor did not refuse it. Verdict (a) FEWER_GROUPS: four of the household's accounts came back as groups, one did not, and one group had no daily point. Verdict (b) DIFFERENT_UNTIED: the returns are not all equal between the two flags across the three compared accounts, yet every group's feeAmount sum is zero, so no account with a fee was compared and the gap is not tied to a fee sum. Verdict (c) ACCEPTED: the flag-false call returned 2xx on the estate's session credential. Pace: six seconds between the two amended calls; no call was retried and no call was made after the second. Reads: two token loads in total, one per run, from Secrets Manager with no refusal; no S3 read and no write.
